```{python}
#| label: fig-esd-pulse
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Typical discharge current waveforms of the ESD models (schematic representation): the 1 kV HBM pulse peaks at about 0.67 A ($V/1.5\\,$kΩ) with a slow decay ($\\tau \\approx 150\\,$ns), while the 500 V CDM pulse reaches several amperes within a fraction of a nanosecond and rings out within a few nanoseconds. Note the logarithmic time axis."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t = np.logspace(-1.3, 3, 2000)   # ns

# HBM: double exponential, rise ~10 ns, decay ~150 ns, peak ~0.67 A @ 1 kV
i_hbm = 0.78 * (np.exp(-t / 150) - np.exp(-t / 5))

# CDM: damped sine, period ~2 ns, decay ~1 ns, peak ~5 A @ 500 V
i_cdm = 8.5 * np.exp(-t / 1.0) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * t / 2.0)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4))
ax.semilogx(t, i_hbm, 'b-', lw=2, label='HBM (1 kV)')
ax.semilogx(t, i_cdm, 'r--', lw=2, label='CDM (500 V)')
ax.axhline(0, color='gray', lw=0.6)
ax.set_xlabel('Time (ns)')
ax.set_ylabel('Discharge current (A)')
ax.legend()
ax.grid(True, which='both', alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
